svg.text: The saving was not in the words. It was in what was written beside them.
One prose file of the Loom documentation site's search index, as it is served. Measured on this branch against its parent.
BEFORE — 5 NOVEMBER, THE SECTION TAKEN OFF THE FRONT OF EVERY KEY
{"under":"/docs/the-runtime","bodies":[
["","The runtime is the half of Loom that runs when somebody asks for a change…"],
["/proposing-a-change#what-the-gate-sees","The Gate reads the delta, not the words…"], …
111 keys in this file, 272 across the five. gzip had already found the shared prefixes; what it could not do was stop them being written.
AFTER — 13 NOVEMBER, NO ADDRESS AT ALL
{"under":"/docs/the-runtime","bodies":[
"The runtime is the half of Loom that runs when somebody asks for a change…",
"The Gate reads the delta, not the words…", …
One body per entry of this section, in the order the browser has had them since the table of contents landed. Empty where a page has no prose.
THE BILL
of 80,000 compressed
79,590 before · 4,356 saved
ROOM IN THE TIGHTEST SECTION
2,335 words
373 yesterday
the shortest page here is 346
WHAT WAS GIVEN UP
nothing
every word still travels
0353's four candidates each gave something up
Taking the section prefix off those same keys, eight days earlier, was worth 341 bytes. Taking the rest of the key was worth twelve times that.
